MolB-RTI vs Skim-RTI vs BrB-RTI — calibrated ancestry-call comparison

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

June 20, 2026

Repo: sawers-rellan-labs/zealtiger

Calibrated cross-validation of ancestry source #2 (SNP50K skim, ~0.4×) against source #5 (MolBreeding target sequencing, ~110×) for the BZea NILs genotyped on both platforms. This is the calibrated successor to the frozen direct comparison (docs/molbreeding_vs_skim.html).

What changed vs the frozen comparison. The frozen notebook compared both platforms at a single borrowed r=8. Here each platform is called at its truth-derived rigidity — Skim-RTI r=5, MolB-RTI r=2 (FP+FN argmin vs the simulated truth; methodology docs/15-rigidity-and-scoring.md), because the two coverage regimes have different physical resolution (docs/14). The Null is the n=1500 BC2S3 simulation (consensus map, no selection) — a modeled expectation, not ground truth: divergence from it is an observation. The per-platform calibration is done in skim_sim_calibration.qmd and gbts_sim_calibration.qmd.

BRB-seq layer (source #6), calibrated. A third real-count platform — BRB-seq 3′ bulk RNA-seq — is layered in. GATK CollectAllelicCounts over the brbseq SNP sites gives REF_COUNT/ALT_COUNT with REF = B73 v5 / ALT = donor, so it is fed to RTIGER as real counts like the others, without the wideseq filter (RNA-seq covers only expressed regions and overlaps the wsfilt panel at too few markers to filter). Its rigidity is calibrated the same way: a benchmark in the measured BRB-seq coverage regime (λ̄ ≈ 2.8×, ~50 % structural missingness, fit from all 379 run_full samples) is swept and scored against truth, giving r=5 (FP+FN argmin — the same coarse rigidity as the ~0.4× skim, reflecting BRB-seq’s low effective coverage). BRB-seq run_full sequenced plates PN1–PN4, so it overlaps the comparison only on the 8 PN4 samples (7 teosinte NILs + the PN4_SID326 B73 check); its sections below are restricted to those, while MolB-RTI-vs-Skim-RTI keeps all 16.

All sites are on the wideseq-filtered high-confidence panel (9,157 v5 SNPs, consistent REF=B73 / ALT=teosinte polarity). All 16 target-sequencing samples are kept (14 teosinte NILs + 2 B73-bulk checks); the 14 NILs are shared with the skim. Calls are RTIGER segments on B73 NAM v5 (name, chr, start_bp, end_bp, state; 0 = recurrent/B73, 1 = het, 2 = homozygous donor). Sample IDs are joined to target-sequencing wells via data/molbreeding_45k_sample_map.tsv (well_id → PN#_SID#); the calls already carry the PN#_SID# names.

Naming (source × caller). Call sets are labelled Source-Caller. Sources: Skim (SNP50K ~0.4× skim reads), MolB (MolBreeding target-capture ~110×), BrB (BRB-seq 3′ RNA-seq). Callers: RTI = RTIGER (per-marker HMM); BIN = BzeaSeq 1 Mb-bin GMM-HMM. So this notebook compares MolB-RTI (r=2), Skim-RTI (r=5) and BrB-RTI (r=5), and (in the Jaccard section) the Skim-BIN reference — Skim-RTI and Skim-BIN are the same skim reads through different filters + callers (50K-SNP RTIGER vs 27M→1 Mb-bin GMM-HMM). The n=1500 simulation is the Null and the breeding-scheme expectation is p0.

Setup

Code 
library(tidyverse); library(GenomicRanges); library(S4Vectors)
source("R/06_score_rtiger.R")
source("R/07_single_locus.R")
set.seed(params$seed)

mb      <- read_csv(params$mb_calls,   show_col_types = FALSE)   # target-seq wsfilt, r=2
skim    <- read_csv(params$skim_calls, show_col_types = FALSE)   # skim, per-taxon r=5
brb     <- read_csv(params$brb_calls,  show_col_types = FALSE)   # BRB-seq RNA, calibrated r=5
gmm     <- read_tsv(params$gmm_calls,  show_col_types = FALSE) %>%   # Skim-BIN (BzeaSeq 1Mb-bin GMM-HMM)
  transmute(name = sample, chr = as.integer(sub("chr", "", chrom)),
            start_bp = start, end_bp = end,
            state = c(REF = 0L, HET = 1L, ALT = 2L)[genotype])
smap    <- read_tsv(params$sample_map, show_col_types = FALSE)
sl      <- read_csv(params$seqlengths, show_col_types = FALSE)
nil_seg <- read_csv(params$nil_seg,    show_col_types = FALSE)   # NULL: introgression segments
nil_co  <- read_csv(params$nil_co,     show_col_types = FALSE)   # NULL: crossover counts

p0 <- single_locus_p0(n_bc = 2L, n_self = 3L)  # neutral breeding-scheme expectation

# common wideseq marker grid, from the filtered RTIGER count files
cf <- read_tsv(list.files(params$mb_counts, full.names = TRUE)[1],
               col_names = c("chr_label","bp","rb","rc","ab","ac"), show_col_types = FALSE)
grid    <- tibble(chr = as.integer(sub("chr","",cf$chr_label)), bp = cf$bp)
spacing <- sum(sl$len) / nrow(grid)

# samples present on both platforms (the 2 B73 checks have no skim NIL match)
samples <- intersect(unique(mb$name), unique(skim$name))
brb_samples <- intersect(unique(brb$name), unique(mb$name))   # BRB-seq overlaps PN4 only
cat(sprintf("MolB samples: %d (all kept) | shared with Skim: %d\n",
            n_distinct(mb$name), length(samples)))

            5*spacing/1e6, 2*spacing/1e6, 5*spacing/1e6))

Code 
# donor blocks from a STATE-segment table (skim, target-seq): merge runs of state>0
donor_blocks <- function(seg) seg %>% arrange(name, chr, start_bp) %>% group_by(name, chr) %>%
  mutate(run = cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(state > 0) != 0)), donor = state > 0) %>% filter(donor) %>%
  group_by(name, chr, run) %>% summarise(size_mb = (max(end_bp)-min(start_bp))/1e6, .groups = "drop")
co_count <- function(seg) seg %>% arrange(name, chr, start_bp) %>% group_by(name, chr) %>%
  summarise(tr = sum(abs(diff(as.integer(state > 0)))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(name) %>% summarise(COs = sum(tr), .groups = "drop")
state_at <- function(df, s) {
  d <- df[df$name == s, ]
  d$state[findOverlaps(GRanges(grid$chr, IRanges(grid$bp, width = 1)),
                       GRanges(d$chr, IRanges(d$start_bp, d$end_bp)), select = "first")]
}

Donor dosage & the B73-bulk control

Per-sample donor dosage (bp-weighted state/2). The neutral BC2S3 expectation ≈ 0.125; a flipped REF/ALT polarity would read ≈ 0.875. The two B73-bulk checks (PN4_SID326, PN6_SID576) should read ≈ 0 — a built-in validity test that needs no external truth.

Code 
dosage <- function(seg) seg %>% mutate(len = end_bp - start_bp + 1) %>%
  group_by(name) %>% summarise(dosage = sum(len * state/2) / sum(len), .groups = "drop")
checks <- c("PN4_SID326", "PN6_SID576")
dose <- dosage(mb) %>% dplyr::rename(gbts_r2 = dosage) %>%
  left_join(dosage(skim) %>% dplyr::rename(skim_r5 = dosage), by = "name") %>%
  left_join(dosage(brb)  %>% dplyr::rename(brbseq_r5 = dosage), by = "name") %>%
  mutate(is_B73_check = name %in% checks) %>% arrange(gbts_r2)
dose
Code 
cat(sprintf("mean donor dosage — MolB-RTI (r=2) %.3f | Skim-RTI (r=5, shared) %.3f | BrB-RTI (r=5, shared) %.3f | neutral p0 %.3f\n",
            mean(dose$gbts_r2[!dose$is_B73_check]),
            mean(dose$skim_r5[!is.na(dose$skim_r5)]),
            mean(dose$brbseq_r5[!is.na(dose$brbseq_r5)]), p0["ALT"] + 0.5*p0["Het"]))
mean donor dosage — MolB-RTI (r=2) 0.083 | Skim-RTI (r=5, shared) 0.062 | BrB-RTI (r=5, shared) 0.054 | neutral p0 0.125
Code 
cat(sprintf("B73-bulk checks dosage (MolB-RTI): %s — expect ≈ 0\n",
            paste(sprintf("%s=%.3f", checks,
                          dose$gbts_r2[match(checks, dose$name)]), collapse = ", ")))
B73-bulk checks dosage (MolB-RTI): PN4_SID326=0.001, PN6_SID576=0.013 — expect ≈ 0

Read: polarity is correct (dosage far below the ~0.875 of a flipped panel) and the B73-bulk checks read ≈ 0 — the built-in control passes. Both platforms read donor dosage well below the neutral 0.125, the donor-homozygote deficit the calibrated three-f_i analysis attributes to biology (skim_sim_calibration.qmd, gbts_sim_calibration.qmd).

State on the common grid

Code 
paired <- map_dfr(samples, function(s) {
  a <- state_at(mb, s); k <- state_at(skim, s); ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(k)
  tibble(name = s, gbts = a[ok], skim = k[ok])
})

Confusion matrix — MolB-RTI vs Skim-RTI

Rows = MolB-RTI state (wideseq-filtered, r=2), cols = Skim-RTI (per-taxon r=5); cell = count (row %). Common wsfilt grid (9157 sites).

Code 
cm <- table(gbts = factor(paired$gbts, 0:2), skim = factor(paired$skim, 0:2))
overall <- sum(diag(cm)) / sum(cm)
prop <- sweep(cm, 1, rowSums(cm), "/")
disp <- matrix(sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", cm, 100*prop), nrow = 3,
               dimnames = list(`MolB-RTI \\ Skim-RTI` = c("0 recurrent","1 het","2 donor"),
                               c("0 recurrent","1 het","2 donor")))
knitr::kable(disp, align = "r",
             caption = sprintf("MolB-RTI (r=2, rows) vs Skim-RTI (r=5, cols): count (row %%). Overall concordance %.3f.", overall))

BrB-RTI rigidity calibration

RTIGER rigidity for BrB-RTI, swept on a benchmark in the measured BRB-seq coverage regime (λ̄ ≈ 2.8×, ~50 % structural missingness) and scored against simulated truth — same FP+FN criterion as the Skim-RTI / MolB-RTI calibrations. r=5 is the argmin (and the donor F1 max).

BrB-RTI cross-check (3′ RNA-seq, shared PN4 NILs)

BrB-RTI state on the common grid for the 8 shared samples, against MolB-RTI (reference) and Skim-RTI. Even at its calibrated r=5, RNA-seq covers only expressed regions at low depth, so treat BrB-RTI as a noisy qualitative read of donor presence, not a segment-resolution caller.

Code 
paired_b <- map_dfr(brb_samples, function(s) {
  g <- state_at(mb, s); rr <- state_at(brb, s); k <- state_at(skim, s)
  ok <- !is.na(g) & !is.na(rr)
  tibble(name = s, gbts = g[ok], brbseq = rr[ok],
         skim = if (s %in% samples) k[ok] else NA_integer_)
})

Rows = BrB-RTI state (r=5), cols = MolB-RTI (wsfilt, r=2); cell = count (row %).

Segment scale & crossover count — MolB-RTI vs Skim-RTI vs Null

Null = the n=1500 simulation introgression segments (nil_segments.csv) and crossover counts (nil_crossovers.csv). For the null, “donor blocks” are the simulated introgression segments directly (no REF segments in that table).

Code 
metrics_calls <- function(seg, lab, nsamp) {
  db <- donor_blocks(seg)
  tibble(source = lab,
         donor_blocks_per_sample = round(nrow(db)/nsamp, 1),
         median_donor_block_Mb   = round(median(db$size_mb), 2),
         median_COs              = median(co_count(seg)$COs))
}
mb_s   <- mb   %>% filter(name %in% samples)
skim_s <- skim %>% filter(name %in% samples)
brb_s  <- brb  %>% filter(name %in% brb_samples)
null_row <- tibble(source = "Null (n=1500 simulation)",
                   donor_blocks_per_sample = round(nrow(nil_seg)/n_distinct(nil_seg$nil_id), 1),
                   median_donor_block_Mb   = round(median(nil_seg$mb), 2),
                   median_COs              = median(nil_co$n_co))
bind_rows(
  metrics_calls(mb_s,   "MolB-RTI (r=2)",          length(samples)),
  metrics_calls(skim_s, "Skim-RTI (r=5)",          length(samples)),
  metrics_calls(brb_s,  "BrB-RTI (r=5, PN4 only)", length(brb_samples)),
  null_row) %>%
  knitr::kable()
source donor_blocks_per_sample median_donor_block_Mb median_COs
MolB-RTI (r=2) 14.0 5.68 22
Skim-RTI (r=5) 5.5 11.51 8
BrB-RTI (r=5, PN4 only) 21.9 0.02 43
Null (n=1500 simulation) 10.3 10.74 33

Read: MolB-RTI resolves more, smaller donor blocks and more crossovers than the coverage-limited Skim-RTI — the high-coverage platform recovers fine structure the skim merges. Both call fewer crossovers than the Null expects (the caller’s segment-merging floor vs the modeled recombination rate); the Null is an expectation, not truth.

Introgression-size distribution

Code 
gbts_b <- donor_blocks(mb_s)   %>% mutate(src = "MolB-RTI (r=2)")
skim_b <- donor_blocks(skim_s) %>% mutate(src = "Skim-RTI (r=5)")
brb_b  <- donor_blocks(brb_s)  %>% mutate(src = "BrB-RTI (r=5, PN4)")
null_b <- nil_seg %>% transmute(size_mb = mb)
ggplot(bind_rows(gbts_b, skim_b, brb_b), aes(x = size_mb, fill = src)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), position = "identity", alpha = 0.5, bins = 30) +
  geom_freqpoly(data = null_b, aes(x = size_mb, y = after_stat(density)),
                bins = 30, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.9, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MolB-RTI (r=2)" = "forestgreen", "Skim-RTI (r=5)" = "purple4",
                               "BrB-RTI (r=5, PN4)" = "orange3")) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "introgression size (Mb, log scale)", y = "density", fill = NULL,
       title = "Introgression-size distribution (calibrated r)",
       subtitle = "MolB-RTI/Skim-RTI = 14 shared NILs; BrB-RTI = 8 PN4; grey line = Null (n=1500 simulation)") +
  theme_bw()

Donor-call composition — het vs homozygous donor

Per-sample het and homozygous-donor fraction of the common grid, by platform. The top reference row is the neutral breeding-scheme p₀ (Het 0.03125, hom-donor 0.10938; single_locus_p0(2,3)) — the expectation under no selection.

Code 
# per-name marker total differs by platform (MolB-RTI/Skim-RTI on the full grid,
# BrB-RTI on its shared subset), so each platform carries its own denominator
tot_gs <- count(paired,   name, name = "tot")
tot_b  <- count(paired_b, name, name = "tot")
comp <- bind_rows(
  paired   %>% transmute(name, platform = "MolB-RTI (r=2)", state = gbts) %>%
    filter(state %in% c(1,2)) %>% count(name, platform, state) %>% left_join(tot_gs, by = "name"),
  paired   %>% transmute(name, platform = "Skim-RTI (r=5)",     state = skim) %>%
    filter(state %in% c(1,2)) %>% count(name, platform, state) %>% left_join(tot_gs, by = "name"),
  paired_b %>% transmute(name, platform = "BrB-RTI (r=5, PN4)", state = brbseq) %>%
    filter(state %in% c(1,2)) %>% count(name, platform, state) %>% left_join(tot_b, by = "name")) %>%
  mutate(pct = n/tot, state = factor(state, c(1,2), c("het","homozygous donor")))

platforms <- c("MolB-RTI (r=2)", "Skim-RTI (r=5)", "BrB-RTI (r=5, PN4)")
# p0 reference row, drawn at the top of every facet
p0_ref <- expand_grid(platform = platforms,
                      tibble(state = factor(c("het","homozygous donor"),
                                            c("het","homozygous donor")),
                             pct = c(p0["Het"], p0["ALT"]))) %>%
  mutate(name = "p0 (breeding scheme)")

ord <- paired %>% group_by(name) %>% summarise(d = mean(gbts)/2) %>% arrange(d) %>% pull(name)
comp_all <- bind_rows(comp, p0_ref) %>%
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c(ord, "p0 (breeding scheme)")),
         platform = factor(platform, platforms))
ggplot(comp_all, aes(y = name, x = pct, fill = state)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") + facet_wrap(~ platform) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("het" = "forestgreen", "homozygous donor" = "purple4")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "% of genome called donor", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Donor calls as % of genome (recurrent not drawn)",
       subtitle = "top row = neutral breeding-scheme p0; BrB-RTI covers only the 8 shared PN4 samples") +
  theme_bw()

Read: nearly every NIL sits above the neutral p₀ on het and below it on homozygous donor — the heterozygote-excess / donor-homozygote-deficit signal, visible on both platforms and stronger on MolB-RTI (which resolves het Skim-RTI under-calls). The calibrated three-f_i decomposition (skim_sim_calibration.qmd, gbts_sim_calibration.qmd) attributes this to real biology, not method bias.

Chromosome painting — all 16 lines, MolB-RTI vs Skim-RTI vs BrB-RTI

Full-genome ancestry painting for every target-sequencing sample: each NIL is one row of three stacked source-method tracks, each labelled at the right of the row — MolB-RTI (r=2) (top), Skim-RTI (r=5) (middle), BrB-RTI (r=5) (bottom); the NIL name runs vertically at the far left. Chromosomes are proportional-width facet columns; segments are painted over their exact start_bp→end_bp extent (geom_rect, not binned). Palette follows the BzeaSeq call_ancestry convention (REF gold, HET springgreen4, ALT purple4). Discordance reads as a colour flip between a sample’s tracks — the dominant pattern is MolB-RTI green (het) over Skim-RTI gold (recurrent), the ~0.4× skim’s het under-call. The two B73-bulk checks (PN4_SID326, PN6_SID576) show a MolB-RTI track only (no Skim-RTI match) and read near-all-gold — the built-in control. The BrB-RTI track is present only for the 8 shared PN4 samples (blank bottom track otherwise). NIL names in bold are flagged LowQuality in the sample-map QC column.

Code 
pal <- c(REF = "gold", HET = "springgreen4", ALT = "purple4")
# B73-bulk checks pinned at the top, then NILs by increasing target-seq introgression
ord <- c(checks, dose %>% filter(!name %in% checks) %>% arrange(gbts_r2) %>% pull(name))

# LowQuality samples (sample_map QC flag) get a bold facet-strip label (markdown)
lowq <- smap$sample_id[smap$quality == "LowQuality" & !is.na(smap$quality)]
name_lab <- function(x) if_else(x %in% lowq, paste0("**", x, "**"), x)

paint <- bind_rows(
  mb   %>% transmute(name, chr, start_bp, end_bp, state, method = "MolB-RTI (r=2)"),
  skim %>% filter(name %in% unique(mb$name)) %>%
           transmute(name, chr, start_bp, end_bp, state, method = "Skim-RTI (r=5)"),
  brb  %>% transmute(name, chr, start_bp, end_bp, state, method = "BrB-RTI (r=5)")) %>%
  mutate(state  = factor(state, 0:2, c("REF", "HET", "ALT")),
         chr    = factor(chr, levels = 1:10, labels = paste0("chr", 1:10)),
         name   = factor(name_lab(name), levels = name_lab(ord)),
         method = factor(method, c("MolB-RTI (r=2)","Skim-RTI (r=5)","BrB-RTI (r=5)")),
         # three stacked lanes per sample: MolB-RTI top, Skim-RTI middle, BrB-RTI bottom
         ylo = case_when(method == "MolB-RTI (r=2)" ~ 0.69, method == "Skim-RTI (r=5)" ~ 0.35, TRUE ~ 0.00),
         yhi = case_when(method == "MolB-RTI (r=2)" ~ 1.00, method == "Skim-RTI (r=5)" ~ 0.66, TRUE ~ 0.32))

# per-track source-method label, placed at each lane's y-midpoint (bottom -> top)
lane_mid <- c(0.16, 0.505, 0.845)
lane_lab <- c("BrB-RTI", "Skim-RTI", "MolB-RTI")
ggplot(paint, aes(xmin = start_bp/1e6, xmax = end_bp/1e6,
                  ymin = ylo, ymax = yhi, fill = state)) +
  geom_rect() +
  facet_grid(name ~ chr, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::unit_format(unit = "", scale = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = lane_mid, labels = lane_lab,
                     expand = expansion(mult = 0.02), position = "right") +
  labs(title = "Ancestry calls — 16 lines × 3 source-method tracks per NIL",
       subtitle = "track labels at right (MolB-RTI / Skim-RTI / BrB-RTI) | gold REF, green HET, purple ALT | blank track = no BrB-RTI",
       x = "Position (Mb)", fill = "Genotype") +
  ggpubr::theme_classic2(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
        # NIL name rotated 90° CCW (vertical) at the far left of each row group
        strip.text.y.left = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 90, hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.05, "lines"),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.05, "lines"),
        # per-track source-method label, horizontal, to the RIGHT of each genome track
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(size = 9), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))

Read: wherever the MolB-RTI and Skim-RTI lanes disagree it is almost always MolB-RTI calling het/donor where Skim-RTI calls recurrent — the coverage-limited skim collapses small heterozygous tracts to background. The B73-bulk checks are near-all-gold, confirming polarity and the caller’s specificity on a known-recurrent genome. The BrB-RTI bottom lane (8 PN4 lines) is sparse and speckled — scattered short blocks rather than the contiguous tracts MolB-RTI resolves, picking up some of the largest donor regions but missing most.

A separate notebook, gmm_hmm_caller_comparison.qmd, brings in the BzeaSeq 1 Mb-bin GMM-HMM caller (Skim-BIN) and compares all three callers (MolB-RTI (r=2), Skim-RTI (r=5), Skim-BIN) on these same 16 lines.

Jaccard agreement vs Skim-BIN calls

Per-sample Jaccard index of donor-present markers (state ∈ {het, donor}) on the common grid, each method against the Skim-BIN (BzeaSeq 1 Mb-bin GMM-HMM on the skim reads) calls as the reference: J = |donor_method ∩ donor_BIN| / |donor_method ∪ donor_BIN|, over grid markers where both call sets define a state. 1 = identical introgression footprint, 0 = disjoint. Restricted to samples scored by all three methods — the shared PN4 NILs (BrB-RTI is PN4-only, and Skim-RTI has no B73 checks), so the three columns are directly comparable on the same rows.

Code 
donor_set <- function(df, s) {                 # grid indices called donor by df for sample s
  st <- state_at(df, s); which(!is.na(st) & st > 0)
}
jaccard_vs_gmm <- function(df, s) {
  if (!s %in% df$name || !s %in% gmm$name) return(NA_real_)
  a <- donor_set(df, s); b <- donor_set(gmm, s)
  u <- length(union(a, b)); if (u == 0) return(NA_real_)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / u
}
# row order: B73 checks first, then NILs by increasing target-seq donor dosage
jac_ord <- c(checks, dose %>% filter(!name %in% checks) %>% arrange(gbts_r2) %>% pull(name))
jac <- tibble(sample = jac_ord) %>%
  mutate(`MolB-RTI` = map_dbl(sample, ~ jaccard_vs_gmm(mb,   .x)),
         `Skim-RTI` = map_dbl(sample, ~ jaccard_vs_gmm(skim, .x)),
         `BrB-RTI`  = map_dbl(sample, ~ jaccard_vs_gmm(brb,  .x))) %>%
  # keep only samples with a Jaccard for all three methods (the shared PN4 NILs)
  filter(if_all(c(`MolB-RTI`, `Skim-RTI`, `BrB-RTI`), ~ !is.na(.x)))
jac %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Jaccard agreement of donor-present markers vs Skim-BIN calls (per sample × method), restricted to samples scored by all three methods.")

jac %>% summarise(across(c(`MolB-RTI`, `Skim-RTI`, `BrB-RTI`),
                         ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Mean Jaccard vs Skim-BIN (NA-dropped).")

Read: Skim-RTI tracks Skim-BIN best — same ~0.4× skim reads, two different callers, so the donor footprints largely coincide. MolB-RTI agrees less by this index even though it is the higher-coverage truth: it resolves het tracts Skim-BIN misses, inflating the union. BrB-RTI is lowest — its sparse, fragmented donor calls overlap the Skim-BIN footprint only partially.

Findings

  • Calibrated rigidity, per platform. Skim-RTI r=5, MolB-RTI r=2 (truth-derived; docs/15), not the frozen shared r=8. The two coverage regimes have different physical resolution, so a shared r over-fragments MolB-RTI (docs/14).
  • Polarity & controls check out. Donor dosage is low (BC2S3-like, far from a flipped 0.875) and the two B73-bulk checks read ≈ 0 — a built-in validity test passed without external truth.
  • MolB-RTI resolves more het and finer structure than the ~0.4× skim, the expected direction; the disagreements concentrate at MolB-RTI-het / Skim-RTI-recurrent sites.
  • Both platforms sit off the neutral p₀ — het excess, donor-homozygote deficit, donor dosage ~0.07 vs 0.125. The Null (n=1500 simulation) is the expectation, not truth; the calibrated benchmarks license attributing the deviation to biology (docs/12-het-excess-diagnosis.md).
  • BrB-RTI (source #6) is calibrated but stays a coarse qualitative layer. Its truth-derived rigidity is r=5 — the same coarse setting as Skim-RTI, because a benchmark in its measured regime (λ̄ ≈ 2.8×, ~50 % structural missingness) has no finer FP+FN optimum. Even so, 3′ RNA-seq covers only expressed regions, so on the 8 shared PN4 NILs it recovers only a small fraction of MolB-RTI donor markers, its own donor calls are largely unconfirmed, and the PN4_SID326 B73 check does not read cleanly recurrent. Useful as a sanity layer for where teosinte is, not as an independent fine-scale ancestry map. ```
